To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AM-T and the retrieval of an event from autobiographical memory are associated with a significant power increase in the delta and gamma frequency bands and with a significant EEG connectivity increase in the delta band.
the retrieval of an emotional memory involves the activation of both low- and high-frequency EEG bands, which are mediated by a complex network.
during the retrieval of autobiographical memories, we observed a complex network of brain regions that is mediated by low- (delta), and high-frequency (theta) EEG bands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the EEG power spectra and connectivity in the context of the retrieval of autobiographical memories.
the analysis of the EEG power spectra and the EEG connectivity during autobiographical memory (Task 1: AM-T, Task 2: retrieval of an autobiographic event).
the modifications of scalp electroencephalography (EEG) power spectra and EEG functional connectivity during the autobiographic memory test and the retrieval of an episodic autobiographic memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AM-T activates a complex cortical network which is mediated mainly by delta and gamma EEG bands.
AM retrieval is associated with an increased delta band EEG power in the left frontal and mid-line areas, and an increased gamma power in the left posterior-midline areas.
autobiographical memory retrieval is a complex phenomenon involving the activation of a wide network, with the engagement of both high- and low-frequency EEG bands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the autobiographical memory retrieval is a complex phenomenon that requires a complex brain network.
the retrieval of autobiographical memories involves the activation of a complex network of brain areas that is modulated by the frequency band of EEG.

the AM retrieval is associated with a widespread increase in delta band power and connectivity, which is consistent with the role of delta band in the generation of slow oscillations and the synchronization of neuronal assemblies, and with the hypothesis of the role of delta oscillations in the consolidation of memory traces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AM-T and the retrieval of a specific autobiographical event are characterized by different EEG modifications.
AM-T and Task 2 are able to modulate brain activity in a different way.

the retrieval of autobiographical events is associated with an increased delta power and connectivity in the pre-frontal cortex, which may represent the neural signature of the cognitive processes involved during the retrieval of autobiographic memories, and with an increased gamma power in the left posterior areas, which may represent an index of the emotional involvement of the memory retrieval.
